A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSAE research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE experiments, ablations, concept-validation results, similarity-search examples, and CelebA analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds BatchTopK comparisons, additional parameter configurations, a comparative concept case study, and feature-stability results.

M1.justification: The nested TopK architecture, weighted reconstruction objective, UW/RW variants, concept-mapping procedure, and optional soft-capping remain unchanged. Section 3.3 expands implementation and inference documentation; it does not establish a new MSAE procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CC3M, ImageNet-1k, CelebA, and vocabulary coverage. The added comparisons and stability analysis use existing tasks and data; the face example extends concept analysis without introducing a new task.

E2.justification: v2 adds BatchTopK as an evaluated competitor in Table 1, Figures 2/11/12, and Tables 6–17, substantially extending comparison against an alternative that also permits flexible sparsity. v1 only cited BatchTopK. JumpReLU is described as an unsuccessful implementation attempt, without reported comparative scores.

E3.justification: v2 extends configurations with ReLU λ=0.01 and TopK k=512, specifies BatchTopK settings, and adds encoder/decoder stability evaluation at expansion rate 8. Appendix B changes the reported preprocessing-bias initialization from the embedding geometric median to zero; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun. Existing splits and training budgets remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix H examines whether learned encoder and decoder directions are stable across training seeds, adding a substantive robustness assessment absent from v1. Figure 8 also adds a comparative face-concept case study across ReLU, TopK, and MSAE. Earlier granularity, modality, soft-capping, and progressive-recovery analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly reports feature stability across training seeds, but gives neither seed identities nor a run count. Standard-deviation plots and ± reporting already existed in v1. The PDFs do not establish an increase in repetitions for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 6–17 substantially expand numerical results while retaining existing rows unchanged. For example, new BatchTopK k=64 results in Table 6 give sparsity 0.877 and FVU 0.162. Table 18 adds stability values, including MSAE RW decoder/encoder scores of 0.437/0.102, and Figure 8 adds qualitative concept-comparison findings. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The SAE objective, hierarchical construction, concept-matching equation, soft-capping definition, and CKNNA mathematics are unchanged. The normalization formula highlighted in Section 3.3 already appeared in v1 Appendix B; no new proof or theoretical result is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: hierarchical SAE learning, improved sparsity–fidelity trade-offs, approximately 0.99 cosine similarity at 80% sparsity, and over 120 validated concepts enabling interpretation and control. Added evidence does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of BatchTopK performance, cross-modal variance, and the relationship between sparsity and feature stability. Section 5.1 interprets the face comparison as showing monosemantic learning specifically in MSAE. Appendix B acknowledges the unsuccessful JumpReLU attempt, while the established applicability and vocabulary limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 announces a code repository and explicitly documents modality-specific normalization and removal of TopK constraints during inference. Basic normalization was already documented in v1 Appendix B. The revised appendix also specifies BatchTopK hyperparameter reuse and changes the bias-initialization description.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of BatchTopK and adds references concerning feature stability, JumpReLU, and concept explanations. It refreshes the concurrent-MSAE acknowledgment to discuss language-model applications. Bibliographic updates and formal citation of the already-linked training blog do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 3.3, Appendix H, acknowledgments, and localized explanations of weighting, baselines, and results. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact; this is not a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: Figures 2/11/12 are redrawn with additional comparator curves and revised legends and axes; Tables 1 and 6–17 gain substantial row expansions, and Table 18 is new. A six-panel face comparison replaces the main-text smile illustration, while the smile evidence remains in Appendix G. These materially change the experimental displays beyond renumbering or pagination.

improvement.justification: Adding BatchTopK addresses an important comparative gap, while explicit inference documentation, the code-access statement, and feature-stability analysis improve assessability. These gains are tempered by unspecified seed counts and a new reporting inconsistency: ReLU λ=0.03 has linear-probe accuracy 0.977 in v2 Table 1 but 0.936 in Table 6, whose value is retained from v1. The net improvement is useful but limited.
